title: Microsoft Entra ID Retires SMS First-Factor Authentication in Favor of Passkeys
content_md: Microsoft is retiring SMS first-factor sign-in across Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenants globally on February 1, 2027, requiring administrators to move affected accounts to passkeys or a phishing-resistant method. The change can interrupt access to Entra-protected applications for accounts that depend exclusively on a phone number and SMS one-time passcode. SMS first-factor sign-in, known internally as SignInNoPassword, lets users enter a registered telephone number instead of a username and password. Entra ID sends a six-digit code by SMS to complete the primary authentication event. Microsoft Entra ID Retires SMS First-Factor Authentication Microsoft is removing it because telephone-based codes are susceptible to phishing , social engineering, SIM swapping, and number reassignment. Beginning February 1, 2027, Entra ID will block phone-number-and-code authentication as a primary sign-in method. Existing SMS configurations will no longer be honored, and Microsoft will remove related controls from administration experiences. Users with another method can continue signing in; accounts relying solely on SMS first-factor authentication risk lockout. The retirement covers Entra ID workforce authentication in worldwide and US Government Community Cloud tenants. It does not apply to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios.
